recipes.name: Alyson's Broccoli Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 head fresh broccoli, cut into bite size pieces

steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside.

In a medium bowl, combine the broccoli, onion and raisins. In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, sugar and mayonnaise. Pour over broccoli mixture, and toss until well mixed. Refrigerate for at least two hours.
Before serving, toss salad with crumbled bacon and sunflower seeds.

raw_recipe.headline: Alyson's Broccoli Salad
raw_recipe.description: Bacon adds a little saltiness to this broccoli salad recipe made with sunflower seeds, red onion, and raisins.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous -- and this from a long-standing broccoli hater! :) Instead of raisins, please use halved seedless red grapes. Have tried both and the grapes are so much better (to us, at least)...in fact, I always add extra. I recommend making this the night before in order for the flavors to meld. You may want to add half the bacon when you make the salad and the rest just before serving so that the salad picks up the bacon flavor but you still get a bit of crunch from the other half of bacon. I use Splenda for the dressing and you can't tell the difference. We did not care for the sunflower seeds. Thanks for the delicious recipe! *UPDATE* Feb 2008 -- Wanted to pass along that I tried using FROZEN baby broccoli florets. Worked great! Bring a pot of water to boil and drop the florets in. Remove as soon as water returns to a boil so the broccoli doesn't lose its crispy texture, then immediately submerge in ice water. Simply just thawing or microwaving for a short time might work even better if you want to retain more crunch. I prefer a little less crunch while hubby likes it very crunchy...I try to find a happy medium. :) If you catch the frozen pkgs when they're buy one get one, could save a little money as well...fresh broccoli can be very expensive. Just be sure to use a quality brand if you try frozen. I used two 1 lb pkgs and made 2x times the dressing (also used extra grapes, onion and bacon). We LOVE this recipe! :-)

Everyone I've made this for just can't get enough! The recipe is so versatile! My favorite is using pepitas and dried cranberries instead of sunflower seeds and raisins. Also, put it in a blender or food processor for a bit and use as a dip! Great!

 Now, years later I've made this dozens upon dozens of times. It is requested at every SINGLE EVENT by everyone. I like a bit of variety, but other people don't. Please be aware that if you make this once, you will have to make it for the rest of your life.

I made 4 servings instead of 6, and the edits I made are so severe that this is technically an alternate recipe: only used 2 slices of bacon, and baked it in the oven instead of fried. Used Walnuts (wife's favorite) and the tiniest amount of red onion. Literally one slice, barely half an inch thick. Used red wine vinegar instead of white. Low-sugar craisins instead of raisins. Turned out fabulous. We are gonna make it again, for sure!

Pretty darn good! Substitutes- honey, apple cider vinegar, and all 3 heads of broccoli that come in the traditional bunch. however i eat all organic and i wonder if organic heads of broccoli are smaller? still saucy with all three heads and yet still devour-able. Tip if you do use honey make sure you mix it with the vinegar first, the acidity breaks down the viscosity and then makes for a nice thin blend to add to the mayo. Fabulous.

Great recipe and my family loved it. I added my own twist by omitting bacon (some don't like it), I used red wine vinegar and steamed the broccoli just for a minute to slightly soften it and make the color pop. I sauteed red onion to take a little of the bite out if it. Like many others, I used red grapes in place of raisins.

Delicious! Only made two changes... I'm not a huge fan of raisins, so I subbed with dried cranberries, and omitted the bacon.

If you're making this for people who don't like broccoli, I suggest cutting broccoli into the smallest pieces you can... with the dressing it doesn't give you that raw vegetable taste!

10/10 would recommend.
Too much mayonnaise. I'd reduce to something closer to 1/3 cup if you expect to look like the picture.

Easy & delish! I soaked the chopped red onion in water for about an hour to reduce harshness. I had no red wine vinegar so mixed some red wine & white balsamic vinegar. I combined dried cranberries with raisins too. Added a bit of salt & pepper. Also used pepitas rather than sunflower seeds.

This is my favorite Broccoli Salad recipe. I have been making it for many years. I use a less mayo than called for (IDK how much less, I eyeball it :-) and make it 24 hours before eating. The flavors meld that way and the dressing gets a bit thinner and the raisins absorb some liquid and plump...I add more sunflower seeds too, as I really love them. I mix the bacon with the salad before putting in the fridge overnight too.

Loved this! Used 2 broccoli crowns, about 1/3 of a red onion, about 1 1/2 cups of sliced red grapes, precooked bacon (it's so convenient!), and the last of a bag of sunflower seeds, toasted. Made the dressing per the recipe except used Swerve instead of sugar. We cannot tell the difference. Put half the crumbled bacon in with the salad to marinate then the other half along with the sunflower seeds right before serving. Hope the leftovers are even better tomorrow!

This is an excellent salad; even the picky eaters loved it. I followed a couple suggestions from others: substituted grapes for raisins and added half the bacon to the salad and let it flavors blend. I made the salad about 7 hours before dinner. I added the rest of the bacon and sunflower seeds just before serving. The salad tastes great the following day too.
I’ve made this for most family gatherings for several years. It’s so easy to make and the flavors are amazing. I didn’t change anything about. It’s perfect as it is !

I love this recipe and so does everyone I serve it to. I did make a few changes I add halved red grapes instead of raisins, add small diced Swiss cheese and cashews instead of sunflower seeds. I know you hate a review that changes things… but this is the way we like it! But thank you for the recipe… the sauce makes all the difference!

I've been making this recipe for years. My family and I love it! I chose this one back then because the sauce uses less sugar than other recipes I saw. I found it on allrecipes.com. It's really delicious. Thanks Alyson!!
Made salad exactly per the recipe. It is delicious and easy. It is a keeper!
You had me at BACON......😁thanks for sharing.
Everyone in the family loves it!
Delicious! We served it at my parents' 50th anniversary. It can be a very wet salad due to the the vinegar, so I recommend letting it sit in a colander a minute before serving.
I used 1/2 broccoli and 1/2 cauliflower and honey instead of sugar. Fabulouse🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
